claim: In July 2008 forward 30-day realized vol rose above VIX (VRP negative) until November 2008, when VIX caught up; VIX then overshot realized in early 2009.
quote: In July 2008, realized volatility on a 30-day, forward-looking basis began to spike over the VIX. This continued until November 2008 when the VIX finally caught up and matched realized volatility.
title: CFA Institute Enterprising Investor: How well does the market predict volatility

claim: Practitioner description: in panics VIX lags the onset of volatility then overreacts (underreaction then overshoot).
quote: VIX is slow to react to the oncoming volatility and then overreacts once it realizes the volatility that is coming.
title: CFA Institute Enterprising Investor: How well does the market predict volatility

claim: Man Group, top 20 VIX spikes in 30 years: if S&P rose in the week after the spike, median first-week return was 1.4% and the second-week average was negative; if S&P fell, mean and median returns were positive at all horizons (equity returns, not vol returns).
quote: However, the pattern reverses if the S&P 500 declines in the week after the VIX spike, as we saw between 29 November and 3 December. In this instance, returns persistence after the second week improves to 86%
title: Man Group Views from the Floor, 14 Dec 2021

claim: Lochstoer & Muir (NBER w28102) model slow-moving volatility beliefs: initial underreaction to vol shocks then delayed overreaction; VIX rises too slowly so VRP falls (search-snippet only, PDF not parseable).
quote: Because the VIX rises too slowly, VIX minus the rational expectation of realized volatility (the variance risk premium) will fall.
title: Lochstoer and Muir, Volatility Expectations and Stock Market Returns (NBER w28102)

claim: Adhikari & Hilliard (2014) find realised volatility Granger-causes VIX, with VIX lagging realised vol by about one month (via search summary).
quote: it appears that the VIX lags realised volatility by about one month
title: The VIX, VXO and realised volatility: a test of lagged and contemporaneous relationships

claim: EFMA paper (2006-2011 sample): VIX futures basis has little forecast power for spot VIX change but predicts subsequent VIX futures returns; buying in backwardation was profitable (search summary only).
quote: the basis does not have significant forecast power for the change in the VIX spot index from 2006 through 2011 but does have forecast power for subsequent VIX futures returns
title: EFMA 2013 VIX futures basis paper

claim: Ing-Haw Cheng (VIX premium): falling estimated premiums predict increases in subsequent realised risk in stocks and VIX futures (search summary only).
quote: falling estimated premiums predict increases in subsequent realized risk
title: Cheng, The VIX Premium (appendix)

claim: Published JFQA/Cambridge paper: VIX is a significant predictor of future realized market variance while VVIX forecasts realized variation of VIX itself (monthly 2006-2016); VVIX is a priced factor for VIX/index option returns (search summary only). It is vol-of-vol, not index-vol, forecasting.
quote: VVIX significantly forecasts future realized variation in the VIX index itself
title: DOI 10.1017/S0022109018001436 (JFQA)

claim: Li & Zinna: total equity VRP is negative with downward-sloping term structure; jump component slopes upward and reacts to extreme events (search summary only).
quote: The total VRP is negative and has a downward-sloping term structure, while its jump component displays an upward-sloping term structure.
title: Li and Zinna, The Variance Risk Premium: Components, Term Structures, and Stock Return Predictability (JBES)
